description: Extend tests/test_ui.cjs to cover the FEAT-002 behavior following the harness's existing vm-sandbox + fetch-stub + click-dispatch patterns, and add a single-invocation live-server probe script under /projects/sandbox that exercises a clear-round cascade and an undo-restore through the real save path. Keep all Python unit tests and the Node harness green.
steps: In tests/test_ui.cjs, add assertions (reusing the existing vm.runInContext / click() helper / fetch-stub patterns; the existing context already stubs confirm:()=>true, so act-then-undo flows run without prompts):

CLEAR-ROUND CONTROL PER STAGE: render each stage and assert the clear-round control exists with the correct cascade copy and data-stage. For To Live assert the rendered round('round1') HTML contains the clear-round control for data-stage='round1' and copy naming To Die & Rebirth; for To Die assert round2Page() contains data-stage='round2' naming Rebirth; for Rebirth assert finalPage() contains data-stage='final'.

EXTENDED ROUND1 CASCADE: call resetStage('round1') in the vm context against the fixture state and assert state.round1 / state.round2 / state.final player goals are all cleared (e.g. all null) while array lengths stay 5/8/10, round1 lineups cleared, and round2 draw reset. Mirror the style of the existing `resetStage('round2')` assertions already in the file.

DISABLED BUTTON SHOWS A REASON (at least one): construct or reuse a view where a primary control is disabled (e.g. a not-ready To Live Submit via view.round1.games[0].ready=false, as the file already does, or a scored game disabling r1-reroll) and assert the rendered HTML contains BOTH the disabled attribute on that control AND an adjacent human-readable reason string.

NEXT-STEP GUIDE REFLECTS `next`: render overview() under at least two different states so `next` differs (e.g. names not ok -> next='settings'; and a complete-To-Live-but-incomplete-To-Die state -> next='round2') and assert the banner text and the data-tab button target match the expected next stage in each case. Reuse the Python fixture helpers already imported in the harness (e.g. fixture(), new_state, round1_lineups) to build the states, following the existing execFileSync-to-python pattern.

UNDO FLOW: simulate a destructive action then undo. With render/flush/save stubbed as the file already does for click dispatch, capture a deep copy of state, dispatch a destructive click (e.g. click({action:'clear-round',stage:'round1'}) or click({action:'clear-r2-game'})), assert the state changed AND the undo snapshot is set (assert the module `undoSnapshot` is truthy via vm.runInContext), then dispatch the undo (click({action:'undo'}) or invoke the undo handler) and assert state deep-equals the captured prior copy and undoSnapshot is cleared. If undo persists via fetch, stub fetch to echo back {state,view,revision} like the existing r2-done test does.
Run `node tests/test_ui.cjs` and ensure it exits 0 with the new assertions; add a console.log summary line for the new coverage mirroring the existing summary lines.

LIVE PROBE SCRIPT: create a shell script FILE at /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh that in a SINGLE invocation: starts `python3 app.py --no-browser --port 8771 --data /tmp/t_easier.json` (flags inside the file, backgrounded), waits for it to come up, GETs /api/state to capture token+revision, PUTs a state that has round1/round2/final scores, then PUTs a cleared state (simulating the clear-round cascade) and confirms via a follow-up GET that downstream is cleared, then PUTs the prior (pre-clear) state back (simulating undo-restore) with the current revision and confirms via GET that the restored scores are present, then kills the server. The whole thing must run as one `bash /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh` call because backgrounded servers die across separate bash invocations and a guard trips on literal port/host flags in the command string. Keep the python server launch and all curl/kill logic inside the script file. Make it exit non-zero on any failed assertion.
Run `bash /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh` and confirm it reports success and exits 0.

Commit the test additions and the probe script on feat/per-match-ranking (note: /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh is OUTSIDE the repo working tree, so only tests/test_ui.cjs is committed; leave the probe script in place under /projects/sandbox). Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_ui.cjs asserts the clear-round control on each of the three stages with correct cascade copy and data-stage.
tests/test_ui.cjs asserts resetStage('round1') clears round1+round2+final while preserving array lengths.
tests/test_ui.cjs has at least one assertion that a disabled control renders with an adjacent reason string.
tests/test_ui.cjs asserts the next-step guide text and its data-tab target match the expected `next` for at least two different states.
tests/test_ui.cjs asserts the undo flow: destructive action sets a snapshot and changes state; undo restores the exact prior state and clears the snapshot.
`node tests/test_ui.cjs` exits 0 and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` stays green (33 tests).
/projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh runs in a single `bash` invocation, exercises a clear-round cascade and an undo-restore through PUT /api/state, and exits 0.
findings:
Added test coverage for the FEAT-002 easier-controls work in tests/test_ui.cjs and a single-invocation live probe at /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh (outside the repo tree). All 33 Python unittests stay green and node tests/test_ui.cjs exits 0. engine.py untouched; no deps added.

tests/test_ui.cjs additions (one new block, 87 lines, mirrors the existing vm-sandbox + click() + fetch-stub patterns):
- (A) Clear-round control on every stage: asserts round('round1') has data-action="clear-round" data-stage="round1" with copy 'Clear To Live (also clears To Die & Rebirth)' and the full-cascade blurb; round2Page() has data-stage="round2" naming Rebirth; finalPage() has data-stage="final" with 'clears Rebirth only'.
- (B) Extended round1 cascade: resetStage('round1') nulls round1+round2+final goals and final results while array lengths stay 5/8/10, clears round1.lineups, and resets round2.draw (revealed 0, order empty).
- (C) Disabled-reason: a not-ready To Live submit (view.round1.games[0].ready=false) renders 'data-match="0" disabled' AND an adjacent class="hint reason" containing 'Enter a score for every player in Game 1 first.'
- (D) Next-step guide for two states: new_state() overview() -> banner with data-tab="settings" and 'enter 10 unique player names'; a round1-complete/round2-incomplete fixture (round2+final goals blanked) -> banner with data-tab="round2">Open To Die and not pointing at settings. Both built via the existing execFileSync->python3 fixture pattern.
- (E) Undo flow: a fresh python fixture is used (earlier sections mutate fixture.state in place via resetStage, so a pristine copy is required). click({action:'clear-round',stage:'round1'}) sets undoSnapshot (label 'Undo: Clear To Live', snapshot preserves pre-clear scores) and clears state; click({action:'undo'}) with fetch stubbed to echo {state,view,revision} restores the exact prior state and clears undoSnapshot. The stub asserts the undo PUT goes to /api/state with restore:true.

Gotchas discovered while writing tests (for future features):
- The undo fetch stub's json() callback runs in the OUTER node scope, not the vm; reference the outer const (undoFix/payload), NOT the vm global `fixture`, or res.json() rejects and performUndo silently leaves state unchanged (caught by the dispatcher try/catch).
- resetStage mutates state in place, so reusing fixture.state across sections corrupts later assertions; rebuild a pristine fixture (JSON from python3) before the undo section.
- undoSnapshot persists across the earlier FEAT-003 reset-all click; reset it (undoSnapshot=null) before asserting 'no snapshot yet'.

probe_easier.sh (single `bash /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh` run, server launch + curl/kill all inside the file): builds a scored fixture state and a cleared-cascade state via python3; starts python3 app.py --no-browser --port 8771 --data /tmp/t_easier.json backgrounded; waits for /api/state; GET captures token+revision; PUT scored (restore:true, since the saved sit-out draw differs from the stored blank draw and the server's draw guard requires it); GET confirms scores; PUT cleared cascade (restore:false — an all-empty reset passes the guard) ; GET confirms To Live+To Die+Rebirth cleared and draw reset; PUT scored again with restore:true (undo-restore) ; GET confirms scores+draw came back; kills the server; exits non-zero on any failed assertion. Confirmed PROBE OK, exit 0.
- Server request shape confirmed from app.py do_PUT: PUT /api/state with header X-Session-Token:<token>, body {state,revision,restore?}; restore maps to store.save(..., allow_draw=data.get('restore') is True). GET /api/state returns {state,view,revision,token}.
